note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old male reporting 3 days of diarrhea with central abdominal pain, intermittent vomiting, and urgency/incomplete evacuation sensation.
- Clinician impression: likely gastroenteritis; advice provided for oral rehydration, self-care, and escalation to in-person GP if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute diarrheal illness (suspected gastroenteritis)
- Timeline: 3 days duration; patient reports symptoms started three days ago and have been neither improving nor worsening.
- Symptoms: frequent loose stools with urgency and sensation of incomplete evacuation; central/peri-umbilical abdominal pain (mild, somewhat relieved after defecation), audible bowel sounds, nausea, one episode of vomiting this morning (after eating fruit).
- Pertinent negatives/positives: patient denies noticing blood in stool; uncertain about low-grade fever—reported sweating over last 4 days but no confirmed fever; no chest pain.
- Examination findings: mild abdominal tenderness on palpation; audible bowel sounds reported.
- Differential / clinician impression: clinician assessment most consistent with gastroenteritis/food poisoning; less likely to represent the bowel cancer described in family history based on current presentation.

Issue 2: Asthma (chronic)
- History: patient reports a diagnosis of asthma; uses an inhaler.
- Medications: uses an inhaler; patient ran out of his usual brand and recently started a new inhaler (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Current status: no acute respiratory deterioration reported beyond baseline asthma; no new chest pain or severe breathing difficulty.

Issue 3: Family history and patient concern for bowel cancer
- Family history: patient states father died of bowel cancer approximately 10 years ago.
- Patient concern: anxious about personal risk given family history; clinician advised current presentation is more suggestive of an acute infective gastroenteritis and less likely to be bowel cancer at this time, with recommendation to pursue further evaluation via GP if symptoms persist or worsen.

Medications:
- Inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- NKDA (patient-stated).

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.

Social History:
- Patient identifies as a foreigner (different brand inhaler purchased here).
- Currently staying at home more due to need to be near toilet; reports inability to attend work while symptoms ongoing.
- No smoking, alcohol, or living arrangement details documented.

Preventative History:
- No preventative care items (cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, FOBT, BMD, vaccinations, optometry, skin check) documented in the consult.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- Abdominal exam: mild tenderness on palpation in the central (periumbilical) region; bowel sounds audible.
- Respiratory exam: no new findings documented; patient reports baseline asthma only.

Plan:
- Advise oral rehydration: drink plenty of fluids to replace losses.
- Symptom monitoring: observe for development of fever, increasing abdominal pain, blood in stool or vomit, persistent vomiting, or clinical deterioration.
- Short-term advice: stay home until symptoms improve.
- Medication: do not start antibiotics (antibiotics not recommended for suspected viral gastroenteritis per clinician).
- Escalation: seek in-person GP or urgent care exam if symptoms worsen or if no improvement after 24–48 hours; patient intends to wait one more day then book GP if not better.
- Follow-up: patient advised to book in-person review if persistent/worsening symptoms or ongoing concern regarding family history.

document_quality (quality checks)
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate), stool frequency and character details, exact vomiting frequency, details of oral intake and hydration status, specific inhaler name/dose/route/frequency, travel/exposure history, recent antibiotic use, smoking/alcohol status, and detailed family history (age at diagnosis of father).
- Internal conflicts from transcript: patient initially stated date of birth as January 1, 1992, then later stated age as 48 years — conflict noted regarding age/DOB.
- Transcript quality: generally intelligible with occasional hesitations and partial repetitions by the patient; no major sections unintelligible.
